content.value_statement: Complex research, development, and testing work needs coordinated agents with clear roles. This skill provides swarm patterns for Claude Flow topologies, workflows, monitoring, and recovery.
actual_capabilities: Explains mesh, hierarchical, star, and ring swarm topologies.
Shows MCP calls for spawning agents and orchestrating tasks.
Provides workflow patterns for research, development, testing, and analysis.
Includes monitoring, memory, fault tolerance, and optimization guidance.
Offers CLI fallback examples for Claude Flow users.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow or compatible MCP tools.
Examples are templates and need project-specific parameters.
Does not install dependencies or verify local tool versions.
Advanced patterns may need human review before execution.

use_cases.title: Coordinate research teams
use_cases.description: Plan parallel research, source validation, synthesis, and report generation with specialized agents.

use_cases.title: Manage development workflows
use_cases.description: Assign architecture, backend, frontend, testing, review, documentation, and deployment work across a structured swarm.

use_cases.title: Scale quality checks
use_cases.description: Organize unit, integration, end-to-end, performance, and security testing through coordinated test agents.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a topology
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to choose a topology for my project. Explain the agent roles and execution order.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a research swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to design a research swarm for this topic. Include gathering, validation, synthesis, and reporting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a build
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to plan a full-stack development swarm. Include architecture, implementation, tests, review, documentation, and deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an active swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the swarm-advanced skill to review this swarm plan. Improve topology, agent roles, monitoring, memory, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Plan a research swarm for evaluating database options.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a mesh topology, researcher and analyst agents, source validation, synthesis steps, and a final decision report.

output_examples.input: Create a testing swarm for a web application release.
output_examples.output: The response separates unit, integration, end-to-end, performance, and security testing, then adds monitoring and reporting steps.
The response identifies role overlap, suggests clearer dependencies, adds monitoring, and recommends topology and workload adjustments.

best_practices: Select the topology that matches task dependencies and communication needs.
Give each agent a clear role, scope, and success criteria.
Use monitoring, memory namespaces, and recovery steps for long workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not assign overlapping responsibilities without a coordinator.
Do not run parallel tasks before dependency order is clear.
Do not use advanced automation without reviewing generated commands and outputs.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps design advanced Claude Flow swarms for research, development, testing, analysis, and operational workflows.

faq.question: Does it require Claude Flow?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples assume Claude Flow MCP tools or the Claude Flow CLI are available.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use the guidance to plan workflows, but tool availability depends on your environment.

faq.question: Does it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and examples. Command execution still depends on the host agent and user approval settings.

faq.question: Which topology should I start with?
faq.answer: Use mesh for research, hierarchical for development, star for testing, and ring for staged pipelines.

faq.question: Is this suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: It is advanced content. Beginners should start with topology selection and simple agent roles before adding automation.
